scopeReview: IMP-6.B.1: location and quality of urban infrastructure, development patterns, politics, social access and environmental burdens. Separates coverage, reliability, capacity, affordability and usable accessibility.
varietyReview: Four assessed stimuli: original access choropleth, fixed-inventory job-access table, outage-hours chart and capacity account. Additional applications examine network benefits, corridor burdens, budgeting, industrial reliability and maintenance.
repetitionReview: Distinct numerators and reasoning demands: rate gap, changing accessibility gap, quality despite full coverage and capacity versus distribution. Varied keys and all-option explanations; no actual city claims or number-only clones. Difficulty is uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Official curriculum and primary UN-Habitat service/access account checked. All question wording, values and geometry are original hypothetical teaching material; no external student resource added and no independent human-review claim.

questions.correctOption: Western households have a 50-percentage-point higher connection rate.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed 90 minus 40 = 50 percentage points, not 50% relative growth. Mapped household denominators are explicit; no count, reliability or causal inference is made.

questions.correctOption: It narrowed from 20,000 to 5,000 reachable jobs.
questions.independentReview: Independently subtracted B minus A: 40000−20000=20000 and 45000−40000=5000. Fixed inventory isolates the accessibility measure, not causation or individual employment.

questions.correctOption: A improved its reliability, while B’s recorded outage hours stayed unchanged.
questions.independentReview: Checked series A[12,3], B[4,4], declines 9 and 0 hours. The chart measures average outage hours, not counts of outage events; the options compare hours only.

questions.correctOption: 4 units/day; the location of capacity and households also affects whether service reaches them.
questions.independentReview: Verified 10−6=4 capacity units/day. Abstract units avoid real engineering specifications, and both quantities use the same daily metric; no treatment-design or health recommendation.

questions.correctOption: A shorter and more reliable trip can connect residents with more workplaces and services.
questions.independentReview: Direct mechanism is changed network accessibility, not a universal economic outcome. No prediction of individual employment or neighborhood income.

questions.correctOption: Nearby communities may face barriers, displacement or pollution exposure that a savings map omits.
questions.independentReview: Omitted dimensions are conditional, not claims of measured harm in an actual city. Distinguishes regional network benefits from neighborhood consequences.

questions.correctOption: Infrastructure allocation is a political and social decision informed by several forms of evidence.
questions.independentReview: No recommendation about a real budget or household. Independent review checked the distinction between complementary evidence and one deterministic ranking.

questions.correctOption: Interruptions can disrupt production and raise costs, with effects varying by activity and backup capacity.
questions.independentReview: Does not apply a universal loss estimate or claim one factor fully determines industry location. Infrastructure quality linked to activity-specific development.

questions.correctOption: Travel cost, usable station access and trips possible at relevant times for different resident groups.
questions.independentReview: Accessibility concerns are supplied in the scenario, not inferred from location alone. Uses aggregate group measures rather than sensitive individual eligibility decisions.

questions.correctOption: Service depends on sustained operation and repair as well as the initial network location.
questions.independentReview: Checked coverage-versus-quality distinction and avoided asserting a quantified lifespan, a particular treatment design or a universal budget priority.

questions.correctOption: New accessibility can influence land demand, while local rules, housing supply and household resources mediate its effects.
questions.independentReview: Conditional mechanism is consistent with official infrastructure scope; no claim that transport alone causes every observed rent change or household outcome.
